# Apply — tokens in the code, one generated file

`/ds4a apply` materializes the resolved layers (core + tone + overlay) into one
CSS file the project imports. It is the only file ds4a writes into `src/`, and
it writes one new file — never edits components, existing stylesheets, or
`tailwind.config`.

## Commands

```bash
python3 <skill>/scripts/apply.py --project .
# → src/styles/ds4a-tokens.css

python3 <skill>/scripts/apply.py --project . --tailwind
# → src/styles/ds4a-theme.css, one @theme block

python3 <skill>/scripts/apply.py --project . --check
python3 <skill>/scripts/apply.py --project . --check --strict
```

Flags: `--out FILE` writes elsewhere; `--tone` / `--type` override the overlay;
`--library DIR` points at another library; `--force` overwrites a file without
the ds4a marker (only after the user confirms).

## What it emits

Plain mode, `:root`:

- `--color-*` for every resolved color.
- `--text-<step>` (font size), `--text-<step>--family`, `--weight`, `--leading`,
  `--tracking` for every type step.
- `--spacing-*` and `--radius-*` from the scales.
- `--shadow-subtle`, `--shadow-elevated` from the tone's prose tables.
- `--duration-fast`, `--duration-smooth`, `--ease-out`, `--ease-in-out`.

Tailwind mode, `@theme`:

- The same values under Tailwind v4 namespaces: `--color-*`, `--font-title`,
  `--font-label`, `--font-paragraph`, `--text-<step>` with `--line-height`,
  `--letter-spacing`, `--font-weight` companions, `--spacing-*`, `--radius-*`,
  `--shadow-*`, `--ease-*`, `--duration-*`.

The file starts with:

```css
/* Generated by ds4a apply — do not edit by hand.
 * Layers: core v1 + tone neutral v1 + project overlay
 * Regenerate: python3 scripts/apply.py --project .
 * Import once: @import "./styles/ds4a-tokens.css";
 */
```

The import line is also printed. Adding it is the human's one job; ds4a does not
edit the stylesheet that already exists.

## --check

Writes nothing. Reports:

1. **Missing** variables — the overlay resolves a token the file does not have.
2. **Drift** — the file has a different value than the overlay.
3. **Stale** — the file has a variable the layers no longer produce.
4. **Candidates** — hardcoded `#hex` and `px` values in `src/` (and `app/`,
   `components/`, `pages/`, `styles/`) that exactly match a token. These are
   migration candidates, not errors: the code may be intentionally outside the
   system, but most of the time it is a value that should become `var(--…)`.

The generated token file itself is skipped, so `--check` stays clean after
`apply`. `--strict` exits 1 when there is any drift or candidate; without it the
command is a report.

## Non-goals for v1

- No rewriting of component files, no codemods.
- No touching `tailwind.config` in place.
- No automatic `@import` insertion.
- One output file per run; a project that wants both plain CSS and a `@theme`
  block runs `apply` twice with different `--out` paths by choice.

The layers stay the source of truth: edit `.ds4a/project.md` or the tone, then
run `apply` again. Hand edits to the generated file are overwritten on the next
run.
